title: The Paperless demo turns on a question that structured data answers and tagging does not
content:
The storyline is compressed into four beats: get structured data from your documents; tag a document as an invoice; "But how much money was spent?"; use the structured data for analytics and for workflow automation.

The third beat is the hinge. Tagging is where document-management tools stop — the document is classified and findable. The question of how much was spent cannot be answered from a tag, only from the fields inside the document, and it is a question every viewer already knows they need answered.

The pattern generalises beyond Paperless: find the question the incumbent's abstraction cannot express, and ask it out loud. It is the same construction as the tool-screen demos, which turn on destroying a record and then asking who approved it.
description: The storyline moves from tagging a document as an invoice to asking how much money was spent — a question a tag cannot answer and structured data can.
